meta.title: Ondra Organ Host
meta.description: The organ ABI host (handbook §8.1, P0): topology, capability allowlist, energy accounting, feedback arbitration, prompt assembly and telemetry. Three non-negotiable constraints live here: C1 organs never write state directly — they only propose via feedback(), and flush() sums every delta per target then applies once and clamps, because applying one at a time makes the outcome depend on organ registration order; C2 organs must pay energy for their own perception and may be refused — consume() is the only door to read state, and when denied=true, state() throws instead of trusting the organ to remember; C3 organ errors must never propagate — tick, toolResult and prompt handlers are each wrapped in try/catch and turned into degraded rather than thrown. The ctx handed to organs is a facade with exactly ten members, never the raw context. Capabilities are default-deny: calling anything not declared raises CapabilityDeniedError rather than failing silently. Prompt fragments carry order, ttl and confidence, sorted by order and filtered for expiry and low confidence; scars are pinned at -1e4 and an organ order below -1000 is refused outright instead of clamped, because clamping would let the author believe their value took effect. Energy accounting defaults to shadow — bookkeeping only — so a week of telemetry can be read before flipping organs to additive one by one, rollback included and no double-billing window ever. No timers are installed: tick() is scheduled by the host, which is what zero-residence means.
